triples.subject: Route
triples.context: Finally, we simulate the route taken by each individual us- ing their assigned transport mode from origin to destination on the corresponding transport network.

triples.subject: ShortestPath
triples.context: We compute the shortest path in terms of travel time for each trip’s origin- destination pair.

triples.subject: DepthDisruptionFunction
triples.context: To account for the effect of water levels on travel, we apply depth-disruption functions [Pregnolatoet al., 2017b; Finnis and Walton, 2008 ]that map water depths on each segment (road, street, cycling lane, sidewalk) to reduced travel speeds and, therefore, increased travel times, or, in the event of trips having no traversable path from its origin to destination, to cancellation of trips.

triples.subject: Flood
triples.context: When a flood occurs, infrastructure is damaged and ought to be re- paired.

triples.subject: DepthDamageFunction
triples.context: Following an initial estimate of the construction costs for each network segment (following the approach by [van Ginkelet al., 2021 ]), we compute the estimated damage us- ing depth-damage functions [van Ginkelet al., 2021 ].

triples.subject: WaterLevel
triples.context: As water levels rise, travel speed reduces, resulting in travel time delays.

triples.subject: EconomicLoss

triples.context: We implement the IAM as a Gymnasium environment [Tow- erset al., 2023 ]in Python and train policies with Stable- Baselines3 [Raffinet al., 2021 ].

triples.context: The case study is Copen- hagen’s inner city, represented by 29 TAZ nodes where one adaptation action per zone can be selected at each deci- sion step, over a planning horizon of 2024–2100.
